title: Cut-and-cover vs bored tunnels
examples: How were the first underground railways built?

figure.name: x-compare

left.title: Cut-and-cover
points: Dig a trench from the surface

figure.verdict: Shallow and simple: cut. Deep or busy: bore

explain.say: There are two main ways to build a tunnel under a city: dig down from the surface, or dig sideways deep underground.

draw.name: x-compare

left.title: Cut-and-cover
points: Dig a trench from the surface

draw.verdict: Shallow and simple: cut. Deep or busy: bore

explain.say: In cut-and-cover, workers dig a long trench, build a concrete box tunnel inside it, then cover it over and rebuild the road on top. London's first underground railway, opened in 1863, was built this way.

draw.name: x-compare

left.title: Cut-and-cover
points: Dig a trench from the surface

draw.verdict: Shallow and simple: cut. Deep or busy: bore

explain.say: In a bored tunnel, a tunnel boring machine digs deep underground and lines the tunnel as it goes. The streets above carry on almost undisturbed, and the tunnel can pass under rivers and buildings.

draw.name: x-compare

left.title: Cut-and-cover
points: Dig a trench from the surface

draw.verdict: Shallow and simple: cut. Deep or busy: bore

explain.say: Cut-and-cover is cheaper for shallow tunnels such as road underpasses, but closes streets for months. Deep metro lines are usually bored, often with their stations built by cut-and-cover.

draw.verdict: Shallow and simple: cut. Deep or busy: bore

faq.a: It is a tunnel built by digging an open trench from the surface, building the tunnel structure inside, then covering it with soil and rebuilding the surface. It suits shallow tunnels.
A bored tunnel is dug entirely underground, usually by a tunnel boring machine that cuts the ground and lines the tunnel with concrete rings as it advances.

faq.q: How were the first underground railways built?
faq.a: London's Metropolitan Railway, opened in 1863, was mostly built by cut-and-cover along existing streets. Later, deep tube lines were bored using tunnelling shields.
asks: How was the London Underground built?

faq.a: It closes roads, means moving pipes and cables out of the way, and only works near the surface. Under rivers, hills or dense city centres, boring is the practical option.

faq.q: Why are stations often built by cut-and-cover?
faq.a: Stations need big open boxes for platforms and escalators, which are easier to build by digging from above, even when the tunnels between them are bored.

facts: The Metropolitan Railway in London, the world's first underground railway, opened in 1863 and was built mostly by cut-and-cover.
The Thames Tunnel, opened in 1843 and dug with Marc Brunel's tunnelling shield, was the first tunnel known to be built successfully under a navigable river.

quiz.say: A new metro line must pass deep under a river and a busy city centre. Which method is most suitable?
quiz.show: Deep under a river and a busy city…
quiz.why: A tunnel boring machine can work deep underground without disturbing the river or streets above.

wrong.1: Cut-and-cover digs from the surface, which is impossible under a river and very disruptive in a busy centre.
wrong.2: An open trench through a river and city is not practical.
